office.title: Indiana State Representative
office.summary: Members of the Indiana House of Representatives write and vote on state laws as part of the Indiana General Assembly. The House has 100 members, each representing one district for a two-year term [1].
duties: Introduces and votes on state legislation as one of the two chambers of the Indiana General Assembly [1].
Must be at least 21 years old when taking office and have lived in the district for at least a year [1].

incumbent.name: Tonya Pfaff
incumbent.summary: Tonya Pfaff, a retired Terre Haute high school math teacher, has represented House District 43 since she was first elected in 2018 [3]. She serves on the Ways and Means and Education committees and is ranking minority member of the Agriculture and Rural Development Committee [3, 4].
record: Committees: Ways and Means; Education; Agriculture and Rural Development (ranking minority member) [4].

April 10, 2025: Voted no when the House passed SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law, 65-29 [5]; she said it "offers very little to individual homeowners while shifting the burden to increased local income taxes" and that Vigo County "stands to lose $20.5 million" [6].

April 2025: Added an amendment requiring consent instruction in human sexuality curriculum to SB 442; after the language was removed in conference committee, it was restored in the final version passed April 23, 2025 [7].
April 25, 2025: Voted no on the 2025 state budget conference report (HEA 1001), adopted 66-27 [8].
Dec. 5, 2025: Voted no when HB 1032, the mid-decade congressional redistricting bill, passed the House 57-41 [9].

2026 session: Authored HB 1325, directing the education, child services, health and family and social services agencies to share data on services for children with special needs; it passed the House 93-0 and the Senate 45-0 and was signed Feb. 24, 2026 [10, 11]. Jan. 28, 2026: Voted yes on HB 1002 (electric utility affordability), which passed 89-4 [12].

race_context: House District 43 is in Vigo County [3]; Pfaff's campaign describes it as covering Terre Haute, West Terre Haute and Seelyville [13].
Wikipedia's 2026 election summary notes Pfaff was re-elected without opposition in 2024 and that Donald Trump narrowly carried the district in 2024 [14].
Pfaff and Lore were the only candidates listed in their parties' May 5, 2026 primaries [14]; both are on the November ballot [2].

Key differences: Pfaff opposed the 2025 property-tax law, the 2025 budget and the 2025 redistricting bill and opposes universal private school vouchers [5, 8, 9, 15]; Lore, a Vigo County school board member, emphasizes reducing administrative paperwork for schools, spending accountability and private-sector job growth [16].
No general-election debate or forum for this race was found.

candidates.summary: Amy Lore is a Vigo County School Board member and former board president with a background in communications and public policy [17, 18]. She is running on school quality, spending accountability and economic growth [16].
background: Elected to the Vigo County School Corporation board in 2020 and re-elected in 2024; board president 2023–2024 [18].
More than two decades in communications and public policy, including as an adviser and speechwriter to former Lt. Gov. Becky Skillman [17].
Indiana State University graduate (bachelor's and master's in public administration); lives in Terre Haute's Farrington's Grove neighborhood [17, 18].
path_to_ballot: Filed as a Republican in early February 2026 [17]; the only Republican listed in the May 5, 2026 primary [14].

items: Wants to improve student results and teaching quality while reducing administrative paperwork and keeping decisions local; says "Every child needs access to high-quality education and the opportunity to succeed" [16].
Supports cost-conscious government with fewer unnecessary rules; says "Hoosiers need practical solutions and responsible spending from their leaders" [16].
Says "Government does not create jobs. It creates an environment where Hoosiers can create jobs" [16].
Wants the state to support local partnerships among residents, institutions and businesses in Vigo County [16].

on_incumbent: No statements by Lore about Pfaff or her record were found; her announcement said she is running to keep state government "focused on serving taxpayers" [17].
plans: Said she is running to strengthen schools and grow economic opportunity [17].
endorsements_finance: No endorsements are listed on her website [19]. No fundraising figures were found.
gaps: No specific positions found on property taxes, vouchers, redistricting, energy or data centers.
No news coverage after her February 2026 announcement was found.
Unverified: a Tribune-Star preview of March 2026 primary forums at the Vigo County Public Library may have listed Pfaff and Lore; the fetched text was inconsistent.

candidates.summary: Tonya Pfaff is the Democratic incumbent, first elected in 2018 and seeking a fifth term [3, 17]. Her 2026 special-needs services bill became law, and she voted against the 2025 property-tax law, budget and redistricting bill [11, 5, 8, 9].
background: Taught high school math for 32 years at Terre Haute South, West and North high schools, retiring in 2025 [3].
Bachelor's degree from Saint Mary-of-the-Woods College and master's from the University of Oklahoma; lives in Terre Haute [20].
path_to_ballot: The only Democrat listed in the May 5, 2026 primary [14].

items: Says "education funding for our schools, Indiana State University and Ivy Tech are the first priority" and that the teacher shortage "must be addressed" [21].

Opposes universal private school vouchers, saying they "take funding meant for the kids in our public schools"; she cites a figure that Vigo County schools have lost more than $36 million since the program expanded [15].
Opposed SEA 1 (2025), saying homeowners' savings would be offset by higher local income taxes and asking, "Of course everyone wants to pay less in property taxes, but at what cost?" [6].
Said the 2025 congressional maps "were not drawn to benefit Hoosiers, but to artificially boost the political performance of one party" [22].
Says "Terre Haute and Vigo County must be aggressive in competing for jobs" and supports expanded vocational and apprenticeship programs [21].
Says local roads depend on adequate state funding and calls for affordable high-speed broadband for every home and business [21].

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. No statements by Pfaff about Lore were found.
plans: Lists education and economic development for Terre Haute, West Terre Haute and Seelyville as her legislative goals [3, 13].
endorsements_finance: No endorsements are listed on her website [13]. No fundraising figures were found.
gaps: No 2026 campaign news coverage or debate found.
No statements found on energy or data centers.
